items.title: Marine Corps Judge Advocate Returns to Mizzou During Homecoming Week to Judge Opening Statements Competition
items.author: SSgt Lennon Dregoiw
items.summary: During the University of Missouri’s Homecoming celebrations, Marine Corps Officer Selection Team Springfield partnered with Mizzou Law to host an opening statements competition to connect with future legal professionals and showcase opportunities available as a Marine Corps judge advocate. The event was highlighted by the return of Mizzou alumnus and active-duty Marine judge advocate Capt. Jeffrey Johnson, who briefed students on military jurisprudence and evaluated the competition. Marine Corps
items.body:
COLUMBIA, Mo. – In the midst of University of Missouri Homecoming celebrations, Marine Corps Officer Selection Team Springfield partnered with Mizzou to host an opening statements competition, highlighted by the return of an alumnus serving as an active-duty Marine Corps judge advocate.

Capt. Jeffrey Johnson, a Mizzou alumnus and practicing Marine judge advocate, returned to his alma mater during homecoming week to give a presentation on the opportunities available as a Marine Corps judge advocate and to judge the Marine Corps opening statements competition. The event gave law students the opportunity to test their courtroom capabilities before legal professionals and Marine Corps leaders in a courtroom environment. Prior to the competition, Johnson hosted a class talk and briefing session. Drawing on his active-duty experience, he provided students with an inside look into military jurisprudence and the daily responsibilities of a Marine Corps Judge Advocate, from prosecuting and defending courts-martial under the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) to advising commanders on operational law.

For Johnson, stepping into the role of evaluator for the opening statements competition allowed him to see the courtroom from a completely different perspective and pass on his knowledge to the next generation of attorneys.

“It was a great experience,” Johnson said. “I have always been on the other side of being either the prosecution or defense, so it was fun to be the judge in this case and give that feedback, using my experience in the Marine Corps and the things I have learned as an attorney to help the students out.”

The competition challenged participants to deliver compelling opening statements in a mock trial setting, evaluating their ability to analyze facts rapidly, build persuasive case theories, and maintain courtroom composure. The unique aspect of this challenge is that it was inspired by real-world scenarios commonly addressed within the military justice system, giving students a rare opportunity to practice military law. “As a law student, there are surprisingly few opportunities to practice giving opening statements, especially if you’re not on the school’s trial team,” said Chase Boggs, a law student who competed in the competition. “Allowing students to get genuine feedback on an opening statement is invaluable. Not only were we able to receive feedback from a Marine Corps judge advocate, but we were able to receive feedback from a Marine Officer who would be on the jury for a trial like this.”

Boggs is no stranger to the military, especially the Marine Corps. The second-year law student at the University of Missouri School of Law is a Marine Corps veteran who attended the class talk with Capt. Johnson before competing in the event. He credited his Marine Corps service and his work in law school for his success in winning the competition.

“Not only was I able to connect with the jurors in the trial, but I was also able to connect with the Marines in the fact pattern,” Boggs said. “Law school has taught me the legal connections necessary to make within the trial, but being a Marine taught me how to connect with Marines.”

Seeing that unique connection firsthand was exactly what made the trip back to Columbia so rewarding for the officer who started it all.

For Johnson, stepping back onto campus during Mizzou’s homecoming added personal significance to the mission. “Being a Mizzou grad, a lawyer, and a Marine Corps Officer, it was great to come back and participate in the opening statements competition,” Johnson said. “It allowed me to speak with the law students, share my experience, and connect with them. I never met with a Marine Corps recruiter when I was in law school, and I wish I had. I love Mizzou and was excited to come and speak with the students here.”

The competition concluded with a plaque being presented to the opening statements competition winner and students sticking around to talk with Captain Johnson and the local recruiters about the Marine Corps Judge Advocate Program. For Officer Selection Team Springfield, hosting these events is about showing law students that the Marine Corps offers immediate, hands-on courtroom experience. Rather than waiting years to lead a trial, Marine judge advocates often prosecute or defend cases right out of law school—a career accelerator that the Springfield team actively works to highlight when looking for the next generation of Marines, next generation of Marine Officers, and next generation of Marine Judge Advocates.
items.titleZh: 海军陆战队军法官在返校节周重返密苏里大学评审开场陈述比赛
items.summaryZh: 在密苏里大学校友返校节庆祝活动期间，海军陆战队斯普林菲尔德军官选拔队与密苏里大学法学院合作举办了一场开场陈述比赛，旨在与未来法律专业人士建立联系，并展示作为海军陆战队军法官可获得的机会。活动的亮点是密苏里大学校友、现役海军陆战队军法官杰弗里·约翰逊上尉重返母校，他向学生介绍了军事法学，并对比赛进行了评审。海军陆战队
zhParas: 密苏里州哥伦比亚市——在密苏里大学校友返校节庆祝活动期间，海军陆战队斯普林菲尔德军官选拔队与密苏里大学合作举办了一场开场陈述比赛，活动亮点是一位现役海军陆战队军法官校友重返母校。

杰弗里·约翰逊上尉是密苏里大学校友，也是一名执业海军陆战队军法官。他在返校节期间重返母校，就担任海军陆战队军法官的机会发表演讲，并担任海军陆战队开场陈述比赛的评委。此次活动让法学院学生有机会在法庭环境中，在法律专业人士和海军陆战队领导人面前检验自己的庭审能力。比赛前，约翰逊主持了一场课堂讲座和情况介绍会。他结合自身现役经历，让学生深入了解军事司法以及海军陆战队军法官的日常职责，从依据《统一军事司法法典》（UCMJ）在军事法庭上提起公诉和进行辩护，到就作战法向指挥官提供建议。
对于约翰逊而言，担任开场陈述比赛的评委让他得以从完全不同的视角审视法庭，并将自己的知识传授给下一代律师。
这是一次很棒的经历，”约翰逊说，“我一直站在控方或辩护方的一边，所以在这起案件中担任评委并给出反馈很有趣，我利用自己在海军陆战队的经验以及作为律师学到的东西来帮助这些学生。

比赛要求参赛者在模拟法庭环境中发表有说服力的开场陈述，评估他们快速分析事实、构建有说服力的案件理论以及保持法庭镇定的能力。这项挑战的独特之处在于，它的灵感来自军事司法体系中常见的现实场景，让学生获得难得的实践军事法机会。“作为一名法学院学生，练习发表开场陈述的机会少得惊人，尤其是如果你不在学校的庭审竞赛队里，”参加比赛的法学学生蔡斯·博格斯说。“让学生就开场陈述获得真实反馈非常宝贵。我们不仅能得到海军陆战队军法顾问的反馈，还能得到一位可能会在此类审判中担任陪审员的海军陆战队军官的反馈。
博格斯对军队，尤其是海军陆战队，并不陌生。这位密苏里大学法学院二年级学生是一名海军陆战队退伍军人，在参加该比赛前曾参加约翰逊上尉的课堂座谈。他将自己赢得比赛的成功归功于他在海军陆战队的服役经历和在法学院的努力。
我不仅能够与庭审中的陪审员建立联系，还能与案情事实中的海军陆战队员建立联系，”博格斯说。“法学院教会了我在庭审中建立必要的法律联系，但身为一名海军陆战队员，我学会了如何与海军陆战队员建立联系。
对那位发起这一切的军官来说，正是亲眼见证这种独特的联系，才让回到哥伦比亚市的这趟行程如此有意义。
对约翰逊而言，在密苏里大学返校节期间重返校园，让这次任务多了一层个人意义。“作为一名密苏里大学毕业生、一名律师，也是一名海军陆战队军官，能回来参加开场陈述比赛，真是太棒了，”约翰逊说。“这让我能与法学院学生交谈，分享我的经历，并与他们建立联系。我在法学院时从未见过海军陆战队招募官，我真希望当时见过。我热爱密苏里大学，也很兴奋能来这里和学生们交流。

比赛结束时，一块奖匾颁发给了开场陈述比赛获胜者，学生们则留下来与约翰逊上尉和当地招募人员交谈，了解海军陆战队军法官项目。对海军陆战队斯普林菲尔德军官选拔队来说，举办这些活动是为了向法学院学生表明，海军陆战队能提供立即上手的法庭实务经验。海军陆战队军法官无需等上数年才能主导庭审，往往刚从法学院毕业就能起诉或辩护案件——斯普林菲尔德队积极强调这一职业发展加速优势，以此寻找下一代海军陆战队员、下一代海军陆战队军官和下一代海军陆战队军法官。

密苏里州哥伦比亚市——在密苏里大学校友返校节庆祝活动期间，海军陆战队斯普林菲尔德军官选拔队与密苏里大学合作举办了一场开场陈述比赛，活动亮点是一位现役海军陆战队军法官校友重返母校。

杰弗里·约翰逊上尉是密苏里大学校友，也是一名执业海军陆战队军法官。他在返校节期间重返母校，就担任海军陆战队军法官的机会发表演讲，并担任海军陆战队开场陈述比赛的评委。此次活动让法学院学生有机会在法庭环境中，在法律专业人士和海军陆战队领导人面前检验自己的庭审能力。比赛前，约翰逊主持了一场课堂讲座和情况介绍会。他结合自身现役经历，让学生深入了解军事司法以及海军陆战队军法官的日常职责，从依据《统一军事司法法典》（UCMJ）在军事法庭上提起公诉和进行辩护，到就作战法向指挥官提供建议。

对于约翰逊而言，担任开场陈述比赛的评委让他得以从完全不同的视角审视法庭，并将自己的知识传授给下一代律师。

这是一次很棒的经历，”约翰逊说，“我一直站在控方或辩护方的一边，所以在这起案件中担任评委并给出反馈很有趣，我利用自己在海军陆战队的经验以及作为律师学到的东西来帮助这些学生。

比赛要求参赛者在模拟法庭环境中发表有说服力的开场陈述，评估他们快速分析事实、构建有说服力的案件理论以及保持法庭镇定的能力。这项挑战的独特之处在于，它的灵感来自军事司法体系中常见的现实场景，让学生获得难得的实践军事法机会。“作为一名法学院学生，练习发表开场陈述的机会少得惊人，尤其是如果你不在学校的庭审竞赛队里，”参加比赛的法学学生蔡斯·博格斯说。“让学生就开场陈述获得真实反馈非常宝贵。我们不仅能得到海军陆战队军法顾问的反馈，还能得到一位可能会在此类审判中担任陪审员的海军陆战队军官的反馈。

博格斯对军队，尤其是海军陆战队，并不陌生。这位密苏里大学法学院二年级学生是一名海军陆战队退伍军人，在参加该比赛前曾参加约翰逊上尉的课堂座谈。他将自己赢得比赛的成功归功于他在海军陆战队的服役经历和在法学院的努力。

我不仅能够与庭审中的陪审员建立联系，还能与案情事实中的海军陆战队员建立联系，”博格斯说。“法学院教会了我在庭审中建立必要的法律联系，但身为一名海军陆战队员，我学会了如何与海军陆战队员建立联系。

对那位发起这一切的军官来说，正是亲眼见证这种独特的联系，才让回到哥伦比亚市的这趟行程如此有意义。

对约翰逊而言，在密苏里大学返校节期间重返校园，让这次任务多了一层个人意义。“作为一名密苏里大学毕业生、一名律师，也是一名海军陆战队军官，能回来参加开场陈述比赛，真是太棒了，”约翰逊说。“这让我能与法学院学生交谈，分享我的经历，并与他们建立联系。我在法学院时从未见过海军陆战队招募官，我真希望当时见过。我热爱密苏里大学，也很兴奋能来这里和学生们交流。

比赛结束时，一块奖匾颁发给了开场陈述比赛获胜者，学生们则留下来与约翰逊上尉和当地招募人员交谈，了解海军陆战队军法官项目。对海军陆战队斯普林菲尔德军官选拔队来说，举办这些活动是为了向法学院学生表明，海军陆战队能提供立即上手的法庭实务经验。海军陆战队军法官无需等上数年才能主导庭审，往往刚从法学院毕业就能起诉或辩护案件——斯普林菲尔德队积极强调这一职业发展加速优势，以此寻找下一代海军陆战队员、下一代海军陆战队军官和下一代海军陆战队军法官。

items.title: Honored Division Week #5: Black Knights return home against Tulane, honor 7th Infantry Division with gameday patch
items.author: Eric Bartelt
items.summary: The Army West Point Football team (2-2) returns to Michie Stadium after two weeks on the road to face American Conference foe Tulane at noon on Oct. 10 at West Point.
items.body:
The Army West Point Football team (2-2) returns to Michie Stadium after two weeks on the road to face American Conference foe Tulane at noon on Oct. 10 at West Point.

The Black Knights take the field this week against the Green Wave, honoring the 7th Infantry Division with division patches on the back of their helmets. The recognition highlights the history, accomplishments and continued service of Army divisions as part of the Honored Division theme featured throughout the 2026 football season.

The 7th Infantry Division represents Soldiers and units stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington.

History of the 7th Infantry Division Known as the Bayonet Division, the 7th Infantry Division began its journey when it was first activated in December 1917 during the height of World War I. Elements of the division saw service during the Lorraine Campaign in 1918.

The division was initially formed by combining Regular Army units stationed around the United States, ranging from Georgia, Texas and Oklahoma to Ohio and Vermont, while drawing its officers from the Regular Army and Officer Training Corps.

Among its early commanders were two West Point graduates: Brig. Gen. Charles H. Barth, USMA Class of 1881, who assumed command in January 1918, and Maj. Gen. Edmund Wittenmyer, USMA Class of 1887, who took command in October. Following the Armistice on Nov. 11, 1918, the division served as an occupation force and conducted training in France before returning to the United States in 1919.

The 7th Infantry Division was briefly posted at Fort Riley, Kansas, and Camp Meade, Maryland, before being inactivated in September 1921, as part of the post-World War I drawdown, although its 14th Infantry Brigade and various other elements remained on active duty.

In July 1940, the division was reactivated at Camp Ord, California, under the command of Maj. Gen. Joseph W. Stilwell, a USMA Class of 1904 graduate. The unit was brought to strength through the first peacetime military draft.

Following the attack at Pearl Harbor, the division transferred to San Jose, California, to protect the West Coast. The division first saw combat in the Aleutian Islands Campaign in Alaska before moving to Hawaii in preparation for the assault on the Kwajalein Atoll. Elements of the division next captured Engebi in the Eniwetok Atoll in February 1944 before moving on to operations in Leyte. In April 1945, the division assaulted Okinawa, leading the attack alongside another Army division and two Marine divisions.

At the end of World War II, the division accepted the surrender of Japanese forces in South Korea before assuming occupation duties in Korea and Japan.

During the Korean War, the division, augmented with Korean troops and American reinforcements, participated in the Inchon Landing, Operation Chromite, with the 1st Marine Division. After liberating Seoul, the division advanced south to link up with units breaking out from the Pusan perimeter.

In October 1950, the 7th Infantry Division conducted amphibious landings along North Korea's eastern coast before advancing toward the Yalu River. Following Chinese intervention, the division fought in the Battle of Chosin Reservoir, suffering heavy casualties. Throughout the remainder of the war, the division participated in several major battles, including Heartbreak Ridge, Old Baldy and Pork Chop Hill.

During the July 1953 battle of Pork Chop Hill, Richard T. Shea, a USMA Class of 1952 graduate, earned the Medal of Honor posthumously. A gifted track athlete at West Point, Shea is also the namesake of Shea Stadium along the Hudson River.

Following the Armistice, the 7th Infantry Division remained in Korea before returning to Fort Ord in October 1974. Although the division did not see combat in Vietnam, it later deployed to Honduras for Operation Golden Pheasant in 1988 and participated in Operation Just Cause in Panama in 1989.

In 1994, the division relocated from Fort Ord, California, to Fort Lewis, Washington, before being inactivated in June 1994. In June 1999, the division headquarters reactivated for a brief period until August 2006. In October 2012, the division again reactivated at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), with the division increasing in strength and capability in recent years.

From the 7th Infantry Division to West Point Capt. Joshua Boylan is currently serving at West Point as a tactical officer for Company H, 2nd Regiment, where he integrates character development for cadets across the academic, physical and military pillars.

“I coach, develop and mentor the cadet chain of command in my company to support daily operations and future planning, ensuring we remain aligned with the West Point Leader Development System outcomes of developing leaders who live honorably, lead honorably and are committed to excellence,” Boylan stated.

Boylan, a West Point Class of 2018 graduate who commissioned in the Field Artillery branch, joined the 7th Infantry Division in May 2022. During his three years with the division, he served as a battalion fire support officer before taking command of Charlie Battery, 1st Battalion, 37th Field Artillery Regiment. His assignments included missions in Thailand and South Korea.

Wearing the division's patch held special significance for Boylan. When he first arrived, his unit wore the 2nd Infantry Division patch and insignia despite falling under the 7th Infantry Division as its higher headquarters. That changed before his departure.

“Late in my battery command, we had an official patching ceremony where all brigades switched to the 7th ID patch, carrying the motto of ‘Trust In Me,’” Boylan said. “The 7th Infantry Division has a rich history of service, particularly in the INDOPACOM AOR (Indo-Pacific Command Area of Responsibility), so it meant a lot to us before we departed for our rotational mission in Korea.”

During his time in 7th Infantry Division, Boylan enjoyed the unit’s missions in the Indo-Pacific region, including those in Korea and the Pacific Pathway missions.

“Each experience required training cycles at the Yakima Training Center, where I spent several weeks alongside my Soldiers, watching them grow in confidence, technical expertise and teamwork,” Boylan explained. “On those missions, we solidified our culture, and we were proud to align our identity with the ‘Bayonet’ Division. Serving in the 7th Infantry Division enabled my Soldiers to play a pivotal role in national strategic defense and work alongside our joint and multinational allies, an experience I will always cherish.

“To add, the joint and multinational planning and execution we did as a member of 7th ID grew my confidence as an officer,” he continued. “It was humbling to learn from allies and partners as I was exposed to great collective professional development for all three years.”

One of Boylan's most influential mentors during his time in the division's Ghost Brigade was Col. Kwenton Kuhlman, who had previously served at West Point in the Simon Center for the Professional Military Ethic.

“He was a great role model and had a major impact on my decision to come to West Point and mentor the next generation of Army leaders,” Boylan said. “He was a driving factor in making it all possible for me.”

Capt. Aleksandr Kauffman, also a USMA Class of 2018 graduate and former Company C, 2nd Regiment TAC officer, is now a full-time student at Fordham Business School.

Kauffman is an Infantry officer who began his military career as an enlisted Soldier at JBLM from 2011-13 when the 7th Infantry Division was reactivated in 2012. During that time, he was a M240 machine gunner and a team leader.

After graduating from West Point and succeeding at his captain’s course, he returned to JBLM, serving with the 2nd Battalion, 1st Infantry Regiment, under the 2nd Stryker Brigade Combat Team, 2nd Infantry Division. The battalion and brigade are now aligned under the 7th Infantry Division.

While serving with the division, Kauffman enjoyed the complex missions the 7th Infantry Division undertook.

“The 7th Infantry Division is constantly modernizing, supporting missions in the Pacific and other areas, and is a rapidly evolving unit,” Kauffman said. “Wearing the patch meant I could take on new challenges, work toward a shared goal, and see my Soldiers and peers excel.”

Kauffman's connections with the division extend beyond his time in uniform. He recalled the Soldiers and leaders he served alongside, including members of the Saturday Morning Coffee Group, as well as the training experiences that left a lasting impression, from exercises at Yakima Training Center to subterranean training and Bayonet Focus.

“I remember one where our battalion was tasked as the opposition forces (OPFOR) for 1st SBCT’s turn through Bayonet Focus,” Kauffman said. “My company faced off against a battalion in the southern training area at JBLM. Many sleepless and rainy nights, but it was incredible watching my company commit themselves to the rep.”

Lt. Col. Timothy Donohue is currently an instructor in Defense and Strategic Studies and the course director for the Academy’s Special Operations Theory and Practice course in the fall semester and Irregular Warfare Theory and Practice course in the spring semester.

Donohue is a Special Forces officer who originally branched Infantry when he graduated from West Point in 2008 as an Economics major.

During his time at JBLM, Donohue served in the 3rd Stryker Brigade Combat Team, 2nd Infantry Division, which was later reflagged as 1st Stryker Brigade Combat Team, 7th Infantry Division. From 2009-12, he served as an infantry platoon leader, company executive officer and battalion assistant S-3.

One of Donohue's defining experiences came when he deployed to Iraq in 2009, just months after taking charge of his platoon. With much of the unit's equipment already shipped overseas and personnel beginning a phased deployment, he relied on the experience of the noncommissioned officers around him.

“The NCOs in the unit had trained, fought and served together as a cohesive team through multiple deployments before I arrived,” Donohue said. “At the time, adversaries and partners overseas recognized units by the patches we wore on our uniforms. It became clear early on in our deployment that our ‘Indian Head’ patch was highly respected. It symbolized grit, determination and lethality to the people who recognized it. I was honored to be a part of that team.”

Serving alongside experienced NCOs and fellow officers left a lasting impression on Donohue, shaping his leadership and building relationships he maintains to this day.

“The NCOs were experienced, professional and technical experts honed by years of deployments overseas,” he said. “They would teach me my most integral lessons in leadership. I also have great memories of serving with exceptional officers during my time there.”

More than a Patch on Gameday Kauffman believes that taking time to recognize Soldiers serving throughout the Army and honor divisions like the 7th Infantry Division is especially important for the Corps of Cadets.

“In a very short time, many of these cadets will be sharing the inside of a Stryker with their Soldiers in the desert mountains of NTC and the rainy forests of JBLM,” Kauffman stated. “Many Soldiers from my previous unit have continued their service and I look forward to these cadets going out and leading these great Bayonet Soldiers.”

Boylan understands the significance of wearing a unit's patch on the football field from both a Soldier's and former player's perspective. He played for Army Football from 2014-17, and during his senior season, he was part of the 10-3 team that defeated Navy, 14-13, in snowy Philadelphia while wearing white 10th Mountain Division-themed uniforms.

As an offensive lineman who played every game that season, he assisted the team in winning its bowl game against San Diego State and set what was then an Academy record of 50 rushing touchdowns in a season.

Now, seeing Army Football honor the division in which he served brings those two experiences together on the gridiron.

“From an officer’s perspective, it is rewarding to see the division you served in worn by the next generation of leaders,” Boylan said. “It offers the opportunity to engage with those cadet athletes and the Corps of Cadets about the significance and rich history about that division, and to tell them how Soldiers can and will watch as they carry the Bayonet Division’s logo onto the fields of friendly strife.

“As a player, I think it gets easy to forget about the significance of representing the logos on a week-to-week basis, but when you can reach down and engage with those cadets about the Soldiers, the locations and operations of the 7th Infantry Division, it provides real insight to the cadet athletes, and they carry much more pride with them into the game, knowing that those they represent will be cheering them on and watching from afar, all over the globe,” Boylan added. “When I played, many of the officer representatives would engage with us like this before each game, and it was awesome for me to think about those men and women deployed watching us carry their brand into our own battles…It truly brings significance to the saying, ‘It is more than a game.’”

( Editor’s note : 7th Infantry Division historical knowledge was provided by Dave Siry, the Director for the Center of Oral History at the U.S. Military Academy.)
items.titleZh: 荣誉师周第5周：黑骑士队重返主场迎战杜兰大学，佩戴比赛日臂章致敬第7步兵师
items.summaryZh: 陆军西点军校橄榄球队（2胜2负）在客场征战两周后重返米奇体育场，将于10月10日中午在西点军校迎战美国竞技联盟对手杜兰大学。
zhParas: 陆军西点军校橄榄球队（2胜2负）在客场征战两周后重返米奇体育场，将于10月10日中午在西点军校迎战美国竞技联盟对手杜兰大学。
黑骑士队本周登场对阵绿浪队，头盔后部佩戴师徽，以向第7步兵师致敬。这一致意是2026年橄榄球赛季全程推出的“荣誉师”主题的一部分，彰显了美国陆军各师的历史、成就与持续服役。
第7步兵师代表了驻扎在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的士兵与部队。
第7步兵师的历史 第7步兵师又称“刺刀师”，其征程始于1917年12月第一次世界大战激战正酣时首次组建。1918年洛林战役期间，该师部分部队曾参战。
该师最初由驻扎在美国各地的正规陆军部队合并组建而成，这些部队分布范围从佐治亚州、得克萨斯州和俄克拉何马州一直延伸到俄亥俄州和佛蒙特州，同时其军官则来自正规陆军和军官训练团。
其早期指挥官中有两位西点军校毕业生：1881届美国军事学院毕业的准将查尔斯·H·巴思，于1918年1月接任指挥；以及1887届美国军事学院毕业的少将埃德蒙·维滕迈尔，于同年10月接任指挥。1918年11月11日停战后，该师作为占领部队服役，并在法国进行训练，之后于1919年返回美国。
第7步兵师曾短暂驻扎于堪萨斯州赖利堡和马里兰州米德营，后于1921年9月作为第一次世界大战后裁军的一部分被撤编，不过其第14步兵旅及其他若干部队仍保留现役。
1940年7月，该师在加利福尼亚州奥德营重新恢复现役，由西点军校1904届毕业生约瑟夫·W·史迪威少将指挥。该部队通过美国首次和平时期征兵补足员额。
珍珠港遭袭后，该师转移至加利福尼亚州圣何塞，以保卫西海岸。该师首次参战是在阿拉斯加的阿留申群岛战役，随后移至夏威夷，为进攻夸贾林环礁做准备。1944年2月，该师部分部队接着攻占了埃尼威托克环礁的恩格比岛，随后又转赴莱特岛作战。1945年4月，该师进攻冲绳，与另一个陆军师和两个海军陆战队师一同带头发起进攻。
第二次世界大战结束时，该师在韩国接受了日军的投降，随后在朝鲜半岛和日本承担占领任务。
朝鲜战争期间，该师在韩国部队和美国增援部队的加强下，与海军陆战队第1师一起参加了仁川登陆，即“铬铁”行动。解放首尔后，该师向南推进，与从釜山防御圈突围的部队会合。
1950年10月，第7步兵师沿朝鲜东海岸实施两栖登陆，随后向鸭绿江推进。中国介入后，该师参加了长津湖战役，伤亡惨重。在战争余下的时间里，该师参加了包括伤心岭、老秃山和猪排山在内的多场重大战役。
1953年7月的猪排山战役中，美国军事学院（西点军校）1952届毕业生理查德·T·谢伊被追授荣誉勋章。谢伊在西点军校时是一名天赋出众的田径运动员，位于哈德逊河沿岸的谢伊体育场也是以他的名字命名的。
停战协定签署后，第7步兵师仍驻留韩国，直至1974年10月返回奥德堡。虽然该师未在越南参战，但后来于1988年部署到洪都拉斯参加“金雉行动”，并于1989年在巴拿马参加了“正义事业行动”。
1994年，该师从加利福尼亚州奥德堡迁至华盛顿州刘易斯堡，随后于1994年6月被撤编。1999年6月，该师师部重新启用，短暂存在至2006年8月。2012年10月，该师在刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）再次恢复现役，近年来该师兵力和能力不断增强。
从第7步兵师到西点军校，约书亚·博伊兰上尉目前在西点军校担任第2团H连战术军官，负责将学员的品格培养融入学术、体能和军事三大支柱。
我在连里指导、培养和辅导学员指挥链，以支持日常行动和未来规划，确保我们始终与西点军校领导力发展体系的成果保持一致，即培养品行高尚、领导光荣、追求卓越的领导者，”博伊兰表示。
博伊兰是西点军校2018届毕业生，被任命为野战炮兵军官，于2022年5月加入第7步兵师。在该师服役的三年间，他先担任营火力支援军官，之后接任第37野战炮兵团第1营查理炮兵连连长。他的任职经历包括在泰国和韩国执行任务。
佩戴该师臂章对博伊兰而言意义特殊。刚到这里时，尽管他的部队隶属于作为其上级司令部的第7步兵师，却佩戴着第2步兵师的臂章和徽章。在他离开前，这种情况发生了变化。
在我担任炮兵连连长的后期，我们举行了一场正式的臂章更换仪式，所有旅都换用了带有‘信任我’座右铭的第7步兵师臂章，”博伊兰说。“第7步兵师有着丰富的服役历史，尤其是在美军印太司令部责任区（印太司令部责任区），因此在我们启程赴韩执行轮换任务前，这对我们意义重大。
在第7步兵师服役期间，博伊兰很喜欢该部队在印太地区的任务，包括在韩国的任务以及“太平洋通道”任务。
每一次经历都需要在亚基马训练中心进行训练周期，我在那里与我的士兵们一起度过了数周，看着他们在信心、技术专长和团队协作方面不断成长，”博伊兰解释道。“在那些任务中，我们巩固了自己的文化，并为自己能将身份认同与‘刺刀’师相契合而感到自豪。在第7步兵师服役使我的士兵们能够在国家战略防御中发挥关键作用，并与我们的联合部队和多国盟友并肩作战，这是我永远珍视的一段经历。
他继续说道：“此外，作为第7步兵师的一员，我们所开展的联合与多国规划及执行，增强了我作为一名军官的信心。在这三年里，我得以接触极佳的集体职业发展，能够向盟友和伙伴学习，这让我深感谦逊。
博伊兰在该师“幽灵旅”期间最有影响力的导师之一是夸顿·库尔曼上校，他此前曾在西点军校的西蒙职业军事伦理中心任职。
他是一位杰出的榜样，对我决定来西点军校并指导下一代陆军领导人产生了重大影响，”博伊兰说，“他是我能够实现这一切的关键因素。
亚历山大·考夫曼上尉也是西点军校2018届毕业生，曾任第2团C连战术教官，现为福特汉姆大学商学院全日制学生。
考夫曼是一名步兵军官，2011至2013年在JBLM以入伍士兵身份开始其军旅生涯，当时第7步兵师于2012年重新恢复现役。在此期间，他担任M240机枪手和小组组长。
从西点军校毕业并通过上尉课程后，他回到JBLM，在第2步兵师第2斯特赖克旅级战斗队下辖的第1步兵团第2营服役。该营和该旅现隶属于第7步兵师。
在第7步兵师服役期间，考夫曼很喜欢该师所承担的复杂任务。
第7步兵师不断推进现代化，支援太平洋及其他地区的任务，是一支快速发展的部队，”考夫曼说。“佩戴这枚臂章意味着我能够迎接新挑战、为共同目标而努力，并看到我的士兵和同僚脱颖而出。
考夫曼与该师的联系远不止于他的军旅生涯。他回忆起曾与他并肩服役的士兵和领导者，包括“周六早间咖啡小组”的成员，以及那些给他留下深刻印象的训练经历——从亚基马训练中心的演习，到地下训练和“Bayonet Focus”。
我记得有一次，我们营被指派担任假想敌部队（OPFOR），为第1斯崔克旅级战斗队在‘Bayonet Focus’中的轮训提供对抗，”考夫曼说。“我的连在刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）南部训练区与一个营对阵。许多个不眠的雨夜，但看着我的连队全身心投入这次演练，真是令人难以置信。
蒂莫西·多诺霍中校目前是国防与战略研究课程的教官，并担任西点军校秋季学期“特种作战理论与实践”课程以及春季学期“非常规战争理论与实践”课程的课程主任。
多诺霍是一名特种部队军官，2008年从西点军校毕业时主修经济学，最初被分配到步兵兵种。
在刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）服役期间，多诺霍曾在第2步兵师第3斯特赖克旅级战斗队服役，该部队后来改番号为第7步兵师第1斯特赖克旅级战斗队。2009年至2012年，他担任过步兵排排长、连副连长和营助理S-3。
多诺霍一段具有决定性意义的经历发生在2009年，当时他被部署到伊拉克，而这距他接管自己的排仅过去几个月。由于该部队的大部分装备已经运往海外，人员也开始分阶段部署，他只能依靠身边士官们的经验。
在我到来之前，部队里的士官们已经作为一个有凝聚力的团队，历经多次部署一起训练、作战和服役，”多诺霍说。“当时，海外的对手和伙伴会通过我们军服上的臂章来识别部队。在部署初期就很清楚，我们的‘印第安人头’臂章备受尊敬。对认得它的人来说，它象征着勇气、决心和杀伤力。我很荣幸能成为那支团队的一员。
与经验丰富的士官和同僚军官并肩服役，给多诺霍留下了持久印象，塑造了他的领导风格，并建立了他至今仍保持的关系。
这些士官经验丰富、专业过硬，是经过多年海外部署磨炼的技术专家，”他说。“他们会教给我最核心的领导力课程。我也很怀念在那里服役期间与杰出军官共事的时光。

比赛日不只是一枚臂章
考夫曼认为，花时间表彰在陆军各地服役的士兵，并向第7步兵师这样的师级部队致敬，对学员团来说尤为重要。
很快，这些学员中的许多人就会在NTC的沙漠山地和JBLM的雨林里，与他们的士兵一同待在斯特赖克装甲车内，”考夫曼表示。“我先前所在部队的许多士兵仍在继续服役，我期待这些学员走出去，带领这些出色的‘刺刀’士兵。
博伊兰从一名士兵和一名前球员的双重角度，理解在橄榄球场上佩戴部队臂章的意义。他曾于2014至2017年为陆军橄榄球队效力，并在大四赛季成为那支取得10胜3负战绩的球队的一员；当时球队在风雪交加的费城身穿白色第10山地师主题队服，以14比13击败了海军队。
作为那个赛季全勤出战的进攻锋线球员，他帮助球队赢下了对阵圣迭戈州立大学的碗赛，并创造了当时学院单赛季50次冲球达阵的纪录。
如今，看到陆军橄榄球队向他曾服役的那个师致敬，让这两段经历在橄榄球场上交汇在一起。
从一名军官的角度来看，看到你所服役过的师由下一代领导者佩戴，是件很有意义的事，”博伊兰说。“这提供了与那些学员运动员和学员团交流的机会，谈论该师的重要意义和丰富历史，并告诉他们，当他们带着刺刀师的标志踏上友好竞争的赛场时，士兵们能够而且将会注视着他们。

作为一名球员，我觉得很容易在一周又一周的比赛中忘记代表这些标志的意义；但当你能够与那些学员深入交流，谈论第7步兵师的士兵、驻地和行动时，这会让学员运动员获得真正的了解，他们也会带着更多的自豪感走上赛场，因为他们知道，他们所代表的人会在全球各地为他们加油，并在远方关注着他们，”博伊兰补充道。“我当球员时，许多军官代表都会在每场比赛前这样与我们交流，想到那些部署在外的男女军人正看着我们带着他们的标志投入我们自己的战斗，这让我觉得很棒……这确实让‘这不仅仅是一场比赛’这句话有了意义。
编者按：第7步兵师的历史资料由美国军事学院口述历史中心主任戴夫·西里提供。

黑骑士队本周登场对阵绿浪队，头盔后部佩戴师徽，以向第7步兵师致敬。这一致意是2026年橄榄球赛季全程推出的“荣誉师”主题的一部分，彰显了美国陆军各师的历史、成就与持续服役。

第7步兵师代表了驻扎在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的士兵与部队。

第7步兵师的历史 第7步兵师又称“刺刀师”，其征程始于1917年12月第一次世界大战激战正酣时首次组建。1918年洛林战役期间，该师部分部队曾参战。

该师最初由驻扎在美国各地的正规陆军部队合并组建而成，这些部队分布范围从佐治亚州、得克萨斯州和俄克拉何马州一直延伸到俄亥俄州和佛蒙特州，同时其军官则来自正规陆军和军官训练团。

其早期指挥官中有两位西点军校毕业生：1881届美国军事学院毕业的准将查尔斯·H·巴思，于1918年1月接任指挥；以及1887届美国军事学院毕业的少将埃德蒙·维滕迈尔，于同年10月接任指挥。1918年11月11日停战后，该师作为占领部队服役，并在法国进行训练，之后于1919年返回美国。

第7步兵师曾短暂驻扎于堪萨斯州赖利堡和马里兰州米德营，后于1921年9月作为第一次世界大战后裁军的一部分被撤编，不过其第14步兵旅及其他若干部队仍保留现役。

1940年7月，该师在加利福尼亚州奥德营重新恢复现役，由西点军校1904届毕业生约瑟夫·W·史迪威少将指挥。该部队通过美国首次和平时期征兵补足员额。

珍珠港遭袭后，该师转移至加利福尼亚州圣何塞，以保卫西海岸。该师首次参战是在阿拉斯加的阿留申群岛战役，随后移至夏威夷，为进攻夸贾林环礁做准备。1944年2月，该师部分部队接着攻占了埃尼威托克环礁的恩格比岛，随后又转赴莱特岛作战。1945年4月，该师进攻冲绳，与另一个陆军师和两个海军陆战队师一同带头发起进攻。

第二次世界大战结束时，该师在韩国接受了日军的投降，随后在朝鲜半岛和日本承担占领任务。

朝鲜战争期间，该师在韩国部队和美国增援部队的加强下，与海军陆战队第1师一起参加了仁川登陆，即“铬铁”行动。解放首尔后，该师向南推进，与从釜山防御圈突围的部队会合。

1950年10月，第7步兵师沿朝鲜东海岸实施两栖登陆，随后向鸭绿江推进。中国介入后，该师参加了长津湖战役，伤亡惨重。在战争余下的时间里，该师参加了包括伤心岭、老秃山和猪排山在内的多场重大战役。

1953年7月的猪排山战役中，美国军事学院（西点军校）1952届毕业生理查德·T·谢伊被追授荣誉勋章。谢伊在西点军校时是一名天赋出众的田径运动员，位于哈德逊河沿岸的谢伊体育场也是以他的名字命名的。

停战协定签署后，第7步兵师仍驻留韩国，直至1974年10月返回奥德堡。虽然该师未在越南参战，但后来于1988年部署到洪都拉斯参加“金雉行动”，并于1989年在巴拿马参加了“正义事业行动”。

蒂莫西·多诺霍中校目前是国防与战略研究课程的教官，并担任西点军校秋季学期“特种作战理论与实践”课程以及春季学期“非常规战争理论与实践”课程的课程主任。

多诺霍是一名特种部队军官，2008年从西点军校毕业时主修经济学，最初被分配到步兵兵种。

在刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）服役期间，多诺霍曾在第2步兵师第3斯特赖克旅级战斗队服役，该部队后来改番号为第7步兵师第1斯特赖克旅级战斗队。2009年至2012年，他担任过步兵排排长、连副连长和营助理S-3。

多诺霍一段具有决定性意义的经历发生在2009年，当时他被部署到伊拉克，而这距他接管自己的排仅过去几个月。由于该部队的大部分装备已经运往海外，人员也开始分阶段部署，他只能依靠身边士官们的经验。

在我到来之前，部队里的士官们已经作为一个有凝聚力的团队，历经多次部署一起训练、作战和服役，”多诺霍说。“当时，海外的对手和伙伴会通过我们军服上的臂章来识别部队。在部署初期就很清楚，我们的‘印第安人头’臂章备受尊敬。对认得它的人来说，它象征着勇气、决心和杀伤力。我很荣幸能成为那支团队的一员。

与经验丰富的士官和同僚军官并肩服役，给多诺霍留下了持久印象，塑造了他的领导风格，并建立了他至今仍保持的关系。

这些士官经验丰富、专业过硬，是经过多年海外部署磨炼的技术专家，”他说。“他们会教给我最核心的领导力课程。我也很怀念在那里服役期间与杰出军官共事的时光。

比赛日不只是一枚臂章
考夫曼认为，花时间表彰在陆军各地服役的士兵，并向第7步兵师这样的师级部队致敬，对学员团来说尤为重要。

很快，这些学员中的许多人就会在NTC的沙漠山地和JBLM的雨林里，与他们的士兵一同待在斯特赖克装甲车内，”考夫曼表示。“我先前所在部队的许多士兵仍在继续服役，我期待这些学员走出去，带领这些出色的‘刺刀’士兵。

博伊兰从一名士兵和一名前球员的双重角度，理解在橄榄球场上佩戴部队臂章的意义。他曾于2014至2017年为陆军橄榄球队效力，并在大四赛季成为那支取得10胜3负战绩的球队的一员；当时球队在风雪交加的费城身穿白色第10山地师主题队服，以14比13击败了海军队。

作为那个赛季全勤出战的进攻锋线球员，他帮助球队赢下了对阵圣迭戈州立大学的碗赛，并创造了当时学院单赛季50次冲球达阵的纪录。

如今，看到陆军橄榄球队向他曾服役的那个师致敬，让这两段经历在橄榄球场上交汇在一起。

从一名军官的角度来看，看到你所服役过的师由下一代领导者佩戴，是件很有意义的事，”博伊兰说。“这提供了与那些学员运动员和学员团交流的机会，谈论该师的重要意义和丰富历史，并告诉他们，当他们带着刺刀师的标志踏上友好竞争的赛场时，士兵们能够而且将会注视着他们。

作为一名球员，我觉得很容易在一周又一周的比赛中忘记代表这些标志的意义；但当你能够与那些学员深入交流，谈论第7步兵师的士兵、驻地和行动时，这会让学员运动员获得真正的了解，他们也会带着更多的自豪感走上赛场，因为他们知道，他们所代表的人会在全球各地为他们加油，并在远方关注着他们，”博伊兰补充道。“我当球员时，许多军官代表都会在每场比赛前这样与我们交流，想到那些部署在外的男女军人正看着我们带着他们的标志投入我们自己的战斗，这让我觉得很棒……这确实让‘这不仅仅是一场比赛’这句话有了意义。

编者按：第7步兵师的历史资料由美国军事学院口述历史中心主任戴夫·西里提供。

items.title: New Kyiv Business Centre opens in Ukraine
items.summary: The inaugural meeting has been held at the centre, which provides a permanent foothold in Ukraine for UK companies.
items.body:
The UK’s first dedicated business centre for industry in Ukraine has now opened, offering companies a permanent presence in Kyiv to deepen industrial ties with our ally.

The Kyiv Business Centre (KBC) is the first of its kind in the Ukrainian capital and is the result of close collaboration between the National Armaments Director (NAD) Group, industrial partners and finance industry, demonstrating the sustained commitment to Ukraine under the 100-Year Partnership.

The KBC gives UK companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), a base from which to build trusted relationships with Ukrainian partners, access battlefield insight and pursue co-development, co-production and investment opportunities.

Until now the cost, security requirements and administrative complexity of operating in Ukraine have made it prohibitively difficult for smaller firms to establish a presence in the country.

Luke Pollard, Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said:

Britain has stood firmly with Ukraine since the first days of Russia’s illegal invasion, and with the Kyiv Business Centre now open, we are helping to unlock new opportunities for investment, growth and long-term recovery. By supporting UK companies in Kyiv, we are deepening the 100-Year Partnership and turning our shared resolve into shared innovation.

Britain has stood firmly with Ukraine since the first days of Russia’s illegal invasion, and with the Kyiv Business Centre now open, we are helping to unlock new opportunities for investment, growth and long-term recovery.

By supporting UK companies in Kyiv, we are deepening the 100-Year Partnership and turning our shared resolve into shared innovation.

The KBC’s operating model is built around three principles: industry, innovation and investment, giving members access to a networking platform to help form partnerships, raise investment and scale-up production and capability.

National Armaments Director Rupert Pearce met with senior industry figures and SMEs to mark the start of the centre’s work connecting UK and Ukrainian industries.

NAD Rupert Pearce said:

This new facility is not just a centre; it’s a permanent gateway transforming the UK’s ability to collaborate meaningfully with our Ukrainian partners now, and for the long term. Until now the costs, security considerations and other restrictions created by Russia’s full-scale invasion have made it difficult for firms, especially smaller firms, to work in Ukraine. Our previous Trade Missions successfully addressed some of those challenges - this centre breaks down those barriers, giving UK firms a permanent centre in Kyiv embedding real opportunities for innovation, investment and export.

This new facility is not just a centre; it’s a permanent gateway transforming the UK’s ability to collaborate meaningfully with our Ukrainian partners now, and for the long term.

Until now the costs, security considerations and other restrictions created by Russia’s full-scale invasion have made it difficult for firms, especially smaller firms, to work in Ukraine.

Our previous Trade Missions successfully addressed some of those challenges - this centre breaks down those barriers, giving UK firms a permanent centre in Kyiv embedding real opportunities for innovation, investment and export.

It builds on more than 40 major UK-Ukraine industrial partnerships already in place and on the success of the MOD’s trade missions to Ukraine. The KBC also supports Ukrainian firms seeking UK industrial partners or establishing UK-based subsidiaries.

UK companies interested in doing business in Ukraine can find out more by emailing enquiries@kyivbusinesscentre.com , or visiting www.kyivbusinesscentre.com .
items.titleZh: 乌克兰基辅新商务中心开业
items.summaryZh: 该中心已举行首次会议，为英国企业提供了在乌克兰的常设据点。
zhParas: 英国在乌克兰的首个专门面向工业界的商务中心现已开业，为各企业提供了在基辅的常设据点，以深化与我们盟友的工业联系。
基辅商务中心（KBC）是乌克兰首都首个此类中心，由国家军备总监（NAD）小组、工业合作伙伴和金融业密切协作促成，彰显了在百年伙伴关系框架下对乌克兰的持续承诺。
基辅商务中心（KBC）为英国公司，尤其是中小企业（SMEs），提供了一个基地，使其能够与乌克兰合作伙伴建立可信关系、获取战场洞察，并寻求共同开发、共同生产和投资机会。
迄今为止，在乌克兰运营的成本、安全要求和行政复杂性，使得较小型企业极难在该国建立业务存在。
国防战备与工业大臣卢克·波拉德表示：
自俄罗斯非法入侵的最初几天起，英国就坚定地与乌克兰站在一起。如今基辅商务中心已经启用，我们正帮助释放投资、增长和长期复苏的新机遇。通过支持在基辅的英国企业，我们正在深化百年伙伴关系，并将我们共同的决心转化为共同的创新。
自俄罗斯非法入侵的最初几天起，英国就坚定地与乌克兰站在一起；随着基辅商务中心如今启用，我们正帮助释放投资、增长和长期复苏的新机遇。
通过支持在基辅的英国公司，我们正在深化百年伙伴关系，并将我们共同的决心转化为共同的创新。
KBC的运营模式围绕三大原则构建：产业、创新和投资，使成员能够接入一个交流联络平台，以帮助建立合作伙伴关系、筹集投资并扩大生产规模、提升能力。
国家军备总监鲁珀特·皮尔斯会见了行业资深人士和中小企业代表，共同纪念该中心连接英国与乌克兰产业的工作正式启动。
国家军备总监鲁珀特·皮尔斯表示：
这一新设施不仅仅是一个中心；它是一个永久性门户，正在改变英国当前及长期与乌克兰伙伴开展有意义合作的能力。迄今为止，俄罗斯全面入侵造成的成本、安全考量和其他限制，使企业——尤其是规模较小的企业——难以在乌克兰开展工作。我们此前的贸易代表团成功应对了其中一些挑战——该中心打破了这些壁垒，为英国企业在基辅提供了一个永久中心，将创新、投资和出口的真正机遇扎根于此。
这一新设施不仅仅是一个中心；它是一个永久性门户，正在改变英国当前及长期与乌克兰伙伴开展有意义合作的能力。
迄今为止，俄罗斯全面入侵所造成的成本、安全考量及其他限制，使企业——尤其是规模较小的企业——难以在乌克兰开展工作。
我们此前的贸易代表团成功应对了其中一些挑战——该中心打破了这些障碍，为英国企业在基辅提供了一个永久性中心，将创新、投资和出口的真正机遇嵌入其中。
它依托于已在实施的40多个重大英乌产业伙伴关系，以及英国国防部赴乌克兰贸易代表团所取得的成功。基辅商务中心（KBC）还支持寻求英国产业合作伙伴或正在英国设立子公司的乌克兰企业。
有意在乌克兰开展业务的英国公司可通过发送电子邮件至 enquiries@kyivbusinesscentre.com，或访问 www.kyivbusinesscentre.com 了解更多信息。

items.title: NMRLC Conducts High-Impact STEM Night Outreach at Yorktown Elementary School
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: A dedicated team of Navy Seabees and Sailors from NMRLC successfully conducted a high-impact STEM Night outreach event at Yorktown Elementary School on Oct. 1.
items.body:
A dedicated team of Naval Medical Readiness Logistics Command (NMRLC) Navy Seabees and Sailors conducted a high-impact Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Night outreach at Yorktown Elementary School on Oct. 1.

Through exceptional teamwork and coordination, the team delivered an immersive, hands-on experience for about 500 students and parents, showcasing critical military and medical capabilities.

The collective effort featured interactive static displays of an ambulance, protective gear demonstrations including the Medium Tactical Vest (MTV) and Kevlar helmets, and a specialized entomology exhibit hosted by Cmdr. Jennifer Simmons, NMRLC's Director for Administration.

Other participants included Construction Mechanic Senior Chief Steven Bussey, Construction Mechanic 1st Class Sean Kelly, Construction Electrician 2nd Class Dakota Black, Hospital Corpsman 2nd Class Kyra Gatt, and Hospital Corpsman 2nd Class Avey Pokorny.

The joint initiative was highly successful, significantly strengthening community relations and inspiring the next generation of STEM leaders. Every member of the NMRLC team played a vital role in this achievement, representing our command with distinction.

Headed by Capt. Christopher Barnes, NMRLC develops, acquires, produces, fields, sustains, and provides enduring lifecycle support of medical materiel solutions to the Fleet, Fleet Marine Force, and Joint Forces in high-end competition, crisis, and combat. At the forefront of Navy Medicine’s strategic evolution, NMRLC is well positioned to be the Joint Force’s premier integrated medical logistics support activity.
items.titleZh: NMRLC在约克敦小学开展高影响力STEM之夜外展活动
items.summaryZh: 10月1日，来自海军医疗战备后勤司令部（NMRLC）的一支由海军海蜂队队员和水兵组成的敬业团队，在约克敦小学成功开展了高影响力的STEM之夜外展活动。
zhParas: 10月1日，一支由海军医疗战备后勤司令部（NMRLC）的海军海蜂队队员和水兵组成的敬业团队，在约克敦小学开展了高影响力的科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）之夜外展活动。
通过出色的团队协作与协调，该团队为约500名学生和家长带来了一次沉浸式、动手实践的体验，展示了关键的军事和医疗能力。
这一集体努力包括一辆救护车的互动式静态展示、包括中型战术背心（MTV）和凯夫拉头盔在内的防护装备演示，以及由NMRLC行政主任、海军中校詹妮弗·西蒙斯主持的专门昆虫学展览。
其他参与者包括建筑机械高级军士长史蒂文·布西、建筑机械一等军士肖恩·凯利、建筑电工二等军士达科塔·布莱克、海军医务兵二等军士凯拉·加特，以及海军医务兵二等军士阿维·波科尔尼。
此次联合行动极为成功，显著加强了社区关系，并激励了下一代STEM领导者。NMRLC团队的每一位成员都在这一成就中发挥了至关重要的作用，出色地代表了我们的司令部。
NMRLC由克里斯托弗·巴恩斯上校领导，负责为舰队、舰队陆战队和联合部队开发、采购、生产、部署、维持医疗物资解决方案，并在高端竞争、危机和作战中提供持久的全寿命周期支持。作为海军医学战略演进的最前沿力量，NMRLC具备有利条件，能够成为联合部队首屈一指的一体化医疗后勤保障机构。

NMRLC由克里斯托弗·巴恩斯上校领导，负责为舰队、舰队陆战队和联合部队开发、采购、生产、部署、维持医疗物资解决方案，并在高端竞争、危机和作战中提供持久的全寿命周期支持。作为海军医学战略演进的最前沿力量，NMRLC具备有利条件，能够成为联合部队首屈一指的一体化医疗后勤保障机构。

items.title: Solving the Unsolvable: Marine Sergeant Earns Meritorious Service Medal for Fleet-Wide Network Fix
items.author: LCpl Alisha Bard
items.summary: CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. — The Meritorious Service Medal is rarely pinned to the chest of a sergeant. Typically reserved for senior officers and staff noncommissioned officers, the military decoration demands exceptional achievement that extends far beyond the scope of a standard billet...
items.body:
CAMP LEJEUNE, N.C. — The Meritorious Service Medal is rarely pinned to the chest of a sergeant. Typically reserved for senior officers and staff noncommissioned officers, the military decoration demands exceptional achievement that extends far beyond the scope of a standard billet. For Sgt. Michael Reta, earning the honor came down to solving a problem that military technicians had written off as impossible.

Reta, a network administrator with Headquarters Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, was awarded the Meritorious Service Medal on Sept. 17, 2026, after engineering a fleet-wide network fix for the experimental Tactical Edge Node-Man (TEN-M) system during Baltic Operations 2026. Maj. Gen. Farrell Sullivan, the commanding general of 2nd Marine Division, personally presented the award to Reta, using his address to the unit to highlight the sergeant's extraordinary technical leadership.

The breakthrough unfolded during the two-week multinational exercise in June, when 2nd Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Battalion received the prototype hardware. The system was designed to deploy dedicated servers directly to the tactical edge, but because the technology was still in its experimental phase, the battalion immediately hit a technical wall when trying to integrate it into the existing operational network.

“The biggest nuance was that there weren’t really any set guides, training, or other units to rely on to see the best lessons learned,” said 1st Lt. Jacob Grubbs, the communications officer for 2nd LAR. “We were starting from scratch.”

With no technical manuals to consult, discovering how the prototype functioned became an exhausting process of trial and error. Where others saw a dead end, Reta saw a challenge.

“My thought process for discovering the answer to this new piece of technology was simple: I used prior knowledge of the networks we already have and implemented the fundamentals of basic networking concepts,” Reta said.

Reta spearheaded the troubleshooting effort from the front. Rather than directing the work from behind a desk, he spent late nights shoulder-to-shoulder with his junior Marines inside server bays, walking them through complex configurations and testing setups line by line.

“He was at the forefront of working through the challenge,” Grubbs said. “Sgt. Reta led from the front, keeping his Marines right alongside him, leveraging his technical expertise, and putting in the extra hours late into the night until the problem was solved.”

After four months of persistent testing, Reta cracked the code. His solution not only brought 2nd LAR’s systems online ahead of schedule, but it also transformed the prototype into a battle-ready asset.

Reta did not stop at fixing his own unit's gear. He drafted detailed technical documentation and shared his network architecture across the fleet, directly supporting testing teams at the Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory to ensure future fielding of the equipment across the entire service.

“When you’re a selfless leader, you’re trying to give the Marines as many resources as possible to execute the task,” Grubbs said. “You shouldn’t be doing things for personal decoration; you should be doing them for your unit and for the Marine Corps as a whole.”

For Reta, the medal represents more than his own long hours in front of terminal screens. “Being recognized with the Meritorious Service Medal means a lot to me,” Reta said. “I see it as a reflection of the Marines and leaders who have supported, challenged, and trusted me along the way.”
items.titleZh: 破解无解难题：海军陆战队中士因修复全舰队网络获功绩服务勋章
items.summaryZh: 北卡罗来纳州勒琼营——功绩服务勋章很少会被别在中士的胸前。这种军事勋章通常只授予高级军官和高级士官，要求取得远超标准岗位职责范围的卓越成就……
zhParas: 北卡罗来纳州勒琼营——功绩服务勋章很少会被别在中士的胸前。这种军事勋章通常只授予高级军官和高级士官，要求取得远超标准岗位职责范围的卓越成就。对中士迈克尔·雷塔而言，赢得这一荣誉的关键，在于解决了一个被军队技术人员认定不可能解决的问题。
雷塔是海军陆战队第2师师部营的一名网络管理员。2026年9月17日，在2026年波罗的海行动期间为实验性的战术边缘节点人（TEN-M）系统设计出一项全舰队范围的网络修复方案后，他被授予功绩服务勋章。海军陆战队第2师司令法雷尔·沙利文少将亲自向雷塔颁发了这一勋章，并在对部队讲话时强调了这位中士非凡的技术领导力。
这一突破是在6月为期两周的多国演习期间取得的，当时海军陆战队第2轻型装甲侦察营（LAR）接收了原型硬件。该系统旨在将专用服务器直接部署到战术边缘，但由于该技术仍处于实验阶段，该营在试图将其整合进现有作战网络时立即遭遇了技术瓶颈。
最大的微妙之处在于，实际上并没有任何现成的指南、训练或其他部队可供依赖，来参考最佳经验教训，”海军陆战队第2轻型装甲侦察营通信官雅各布·格拉布斯中尉说，“我们是从零开始。
由于没有技术手册可供查阅，弄清这个原型如何运作便成了一段令人精疲力竭的试错过程。在别人看到死路的地方，雷塔看到的却是挑战。
我找到这项新技术答案的思路很简单：我利用了对我们已有网络的既有了解，并应用了基础网络概念的基本原理，”雷塔说。
雷塔身先士卒，带头推进故障排查工作。他没有坐在办公桌后指挥，而是与手下的初级海军陆战队员在服务器舱内并肩熬到深夜，逐行带他们梳理复杂配置并测试各项设置。
他在攻克这一挑战的过程中始终冲在最前面，”格鲁布斯说。“雷塔中士身先士卒，让自己的海军陆战队员紧随左右，发挥自身技术专长，并加班到深夜，直到问题得到解决。
经过四个月坚持不懈的测试，雷塔终于破解了难题。他的解决方案不仅让第2轻装甲侦察营的系统提前上线，还将这一原型转化为可投入战斗的资产。
雷塔并未止步于修复本单位的装备。他编写了详细的技术文档，并在整个舰队范围内分享了自己的网络架构，直接支持了海军陆战队作战实验室的测试团队，以确保该装备未来在整个军种内列装。
当你是一名无私的领导者时，你会努力为海军陆战队员提供尽可能多的资源来执行任务，”格拉布斯说。“你不应该为了个人勋章而做事；你应该为你的单位和整个海军陆战队而做事。
对雷塔而言，这枚奖章所代表的不仅仅是他自己在终端屏幕前长时间工作。“获得功绩服役奖章这份认可，对我意义重大，”雷塔说。“我认为，它折射出一路走来支持我、挑战我并信任我的海军陆战队员和领导们。

items.title: Reel: Prime Hall speaks on overcoming challenges
items.author: Cpl Diego Berumen
items.summary: Retired U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Prime Hall, a former Marine raider and a human performance coach, speaks about overcoming challenges at San Clemente, California, September 29, 2026. Hall uses the skills and discipline he learned during his time in the Marine Corps to not only overcome his own tribulations, but to help others overcome their own fears and challenges. Hall is a native of Texas.

items.title: ‘Engine’ behind Fort Jackson welcomes new CSM
items.author: Robert Timmons
items.summary: U.S. Army Garrison – Fort Jackson bid farewell to one senior enlisted advisor and welcomed another during a ceremony held Oct. 6 at Victory Field. Command Sgt. Maj. Brie Kotula passed responsibility for Fort Jackson’s garrison to Command Sgt. Maj. Hector Rodriguezpabon during the ceremony.
items.body: U.S. Army Garrison – Fort Jackson bid farewell to one senior enlisted advisor and welcomed another during a ceremony held Oct. 6 at Victory Field. Command Sgt. Maj. Brie Kotula passed responsibility for Fort Jackson’s garrison to Command Sgt. Maj. Hector Rodriguezpabon during the ceremony. The ceremony is an enactment of a 251-year-old Army tradition steeped in time-honored values and traditions. The key part of the ceremony is the passing of the unit colors symbolizing the seamless transfer of responsibility and unwavering care for Soldiers, Department of the Army Civilians, and families of the garrison. Col. David Gaugush, garrison commander, lauded Kotula for her efforts to help the Fort Jackson community. “I could count on your candor,” he said. “You were always steadfast in your commitment to the mission, and your first thought was always concerning our garrison teammates. you stayed true to who you are as a person and a professional, always. “As a Garrison CSM, you’ve been involved in a wide range of actions and events and accomplishments, but that all quickly fades with time. Your legacy and what is truly important is how you impacted the lives around you, and everything else just pales in comparison.” He added she was a prime example of how to lead and to teach others – through coaching and validation. “That’s how you develop people,” he said. “That’s what we expect of our (noncommissioned officer) corps. You don’t make them dependent on you. You teach them. You trust them, and then you give them the confidence to stand on their own. And Brie did that for people across this organization. Sometimes that leadership showed up in much more personal ways.” Kotula, who is retiring and becoming a Richland County Sheriff’s Deputy, said she was humbled by her experiences. “Standing here today,” she said, “I find myself filled with a mix of immense gratitude, a touch of nostalgia, profound pride as I look across the crowd and see the people who have made the last few years the highlight of my career … “When people think of the Army, they often picture boots in the dirt, tactical gear, and field training, but as a garrison CSM, you quickly learn that an installation is like a city, and running a city requires a different kind of dedication. To the incredible directorates, the leaders, the Soldiers, and especially our DA civilians and workforce, thank you. You are truly the heartbeat of this installation.” She added she felt confident that her successor will prosper in his new role. “Hector, you are inheriting on of the best installations in the Army, backed by an unmatched team,” Kotula said. “Handing over the guidon today gives me complete peace of mind and knowing you are stepping into the role. Lean on the civilian directors, trust your instincts, and take care of the workforce. They will take care of you …” Rodriguezpabon is no stranger to Fort Jackson as he completed Basic Combat Training here on his way to being a 92A – Automated Logistical Specialist. He has served in every leadership position an enlisted Soldier can during his more than 23 years in the Army. He comes to Fort Jackson from the 87th Division Sustainment Support Battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia. “Fort Jackson is where my story began,” he said. “It is where I was forged. To return here now, 23 years later, as your garrison command sergeant major is an honor of a lifetime.” He told his new boss that he was looking forward to working with him. “As your senior enlisted advisor,” he said to Gaugush, “I’m committed to working shoulder to shoulder with you every single day to ensure this installation remains a premier platform for power projection training and quality of life.” He also thanked Kotula for the groundwork she paved with the unit. “Thank you for your exceptional stewardship, your energy, and the standard of excellence you establish across the Fort Jackson footprint,” he said. “You have left large boots to fill, but because of the foundation you and your team build, we are positioned for continued success.” Finally, he thanked the garrison for its work in helping make American Soldiers. “To the men and women of U.S. Army Garrison - Fort Jackson, the Soldiers, Civilians, contractors, and volunteers, you are the engine behind everything that happens here,” he said. “I look forward to visiting your work areas and offices, getting to know each of you, and continuing to build this exceptional team.

items.title: AMLC, 6th MLMC team honors fallen firefighters during 9/11 memorial stair climb
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: FREDERICK, Md. – Carrying the Army’s commitment to honoring the fallen, community service and physical readiness, a joint team of Soldiers and civilians from U.S. Army Medical Logistics Command and the 6th Medical Logistics Management Center raised over $1,000 for the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation during the 9/11 Remembrance Stair Climb at Harry Grove Stadium on Sept. 24.
items.body:
By Maj. Antonio Acevedo-Guzman

FREDERICK, Md. – Carrying the Army’s commitment to honoring the fallen, community service and physical readiness, a joint team of Soldiers and civilians from U.S. Army Medical Logistics Command and the 6th Medical Logistics Management Center raised over $1,000 for the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation during the 9/11 Remembrance Stair Climb at Harry Grove Stadium on Sept. 24.

Staff Sgt. Eduardo Gomez, an operations noncommissioned officer with AMLC and a student in the Long-Term Health Education and Training program, led the nine-member MEDLOG team from nearby Fort Detrick, earning second place among all participating groups for total charitable contributions.

The National Fallen Firefighters Foundation provides critical resources, college scholarships and peer networks to the families of fallen firefighters nationwide, in addition to supporting counseling programs for the Fire Department of New York.

For the participants, the event was a demanding physical test designed to honor the ultimate sacrifice made by more than 400 first responders on Sept. 11, 2001, including FDNY firefighters, law enforcement personnel and emergency medical technicians.

Climbers completed seven circuits across the stadium bowl, ascending and descending concrete stairs to equal the 110 stories of the World Trade Center towers.

“Climbing 110 flights is a gut check that demands physical endurance and mental toughness – the very same traits we embody through our Warrior Ethos,” said Gomez, who also volunteers as a firefighter with Frederick’s Independent Hose Co., Station 1. “I volunteer to give back to our neighbors, but stepping into the stadium alongside our teammates was about honoring those who charged up those tower steps that day without hesitation.”

While the climb served as a solemn tribute, it also reinforced operational readiness. Medical logisticians are tasked with sustaining the force across multidomain operations, a mission that demands planning and mental resilience to distribute life-saving medical equipment and supplies in contested, austere environments.

By pushing through the exhaustion to cross the stadium finish line together, AMLC and 6th MLMC personnel reinforced the enduring bond between the Army and civilian first responders who protect American communities and safeguard the homeland.

“This event tested our stamina, while reinforcing our esprit de corps and proving that readiness extends beyond our daily desk duties into our activities outside work and into the communities we support,” Gomez said.

Headquartered at Fort Detrick, AMLC serves as the Army's Class VIII medical materiel command, delivering integrated medical logistics that enables Army and Joint Forces readiness from the strategic support area to the tactical edge.

The 6th MLMC, also headquartered at Detrick, is a specialized unit that utilizes split-based operations to provide forward and centralized medical materiel management, theater-level distribution tracking and operational logistical synchronization in support of combatant commanders across the globe.
items.titleZh: 美国陆军医疗后勤司令部与第6医疗后勤管理中心团队在9·11纪念登楼活动中缅怀殉职消防员
items.summaryZh: 马里兰州弗雷德里克——秉承陆军缅怀阵亡者、服务社区和保持体能战备的承诺，来自美国陆军医疗后勤司令部和第6医疗后勤管理中心的军人与文职人员联合团队，在9月24日于哈里·格罗夫体育场举行的9·11纪念登楼活动中，为国家殉职消防员基金会筹集了超过1000美元。
zhParas: 作者：安东尼奥·阿塞维多-古兹曼少校
马里兰州弗雷德里克——秉承美国陆军缅怀殉职者、服务社区和保持体能战备的承诺，一支由美国陆军医疗后勤司令部与第6医疗后勤管理中心军人及文职人员组成的联合团队，于9月24日在哈里格罗夫体育场举行的9·11纪念登楼活动中，为国家殉职消防员基金会筹集了超过1000美元。
美国陆军医疗后勤司令部（AMLC）作战军士、长期健康教育训练项目学员爱德华多·戈麦斯上士，带领来自附近德特里克堡的九人医疗后勤团队，其慈善捐款总额在全部参赛队伍中排名第二。
全国殉职消防员基金会为全美殉职消防员的家属提供关键资源、大学奖学金和同伴互助网络，此外还支持纽约市消防局的心理咨询项目。
对参与者而言，这项活动是一场高强度的体能考验，旨在纪念2001年9月11日400多名应急救援人员所做出的最大牺牲，其中包括纽约市消防局消防员、执法人员及急救医疗技术人员。
攀登者绕体育场碗形看台完成七圈，上下混凝土楼梯，累计高度相当于世界贸易中心双塔的110层。
攀登110层楼梯是一次极限考验，需要体能耐力和心理韧性——这正是我们通过勇士精神所展现的特质，”戈麦斯说。他还在弗雷德里克独立消防队1号站担任志愿消防员。“我做志愿者是为了回馈邻里，但与队友一起走进体育场，是为了纪念那天毫不犹豫冲上塔楼楼梯的人们。
这次攀登既是一次庄严的致敬，也强化了作战战备。医疗后勤人员肩负着在多域作战中为部队提供持续保障的任务，这一使命要求在争夺激烈、条件严酷的环境中分发救生医疗设备与物资时具备规划能力和心理韧性。
AMLC和第六医疗后勤管理中心人员克服疲惫，共同冲过体育场终点线，从而进一步巩固了陆军与保护美国社区、守护国土的平民一线应急人员之间历久弥坚的纽带。
这次活动考验了我们的耐力，同时增强了我们的团队精神，并证明战备不仅限于我们日常的案头工作，还延伸到我们工作之外的活动以及我们所支持的社区，”戈麦斯说。
AMLC总部位于德特里克堡，是陆军的第八类医疗物资司令部，提供一体化医疗后勤，支撑陆军和联合部队从战略支援区域到战术前沿的战备。
第6医疗后勤管理中心也总部位于德特里克堡，是一支专业部队，采用分基地行动，提供前沿和集中化医疗物资管理、战区级配送跟踪以及作战后勤同步，以支援全球各地的作战指挥官。

全国殉职消防员基金会为全美殉职消防员的家属提供关键资源、大学奖学金和同伴互助网络，此外还支持纽约市消防局的心理咨询项目。

对参与者而言，这项活动是一场高强度的体能考验，旨在纪念2001年9月11日400多名应急救援人员所做出的最大牺牲，其中包括纽约市消防局消防员、执法人员及急救医疗技术人员。

攀登者绕体育场碗形看台完成七圈，上下混凝土楼梯，累计高度相当于世界贸易中心双塔的110层。

攀登110层楼梯是一次极限考验，需要体能耐力和心理韧性——这正是我们通过勇士精神所展现的特质，”戈麦斯说。他还在弗雷德里克独立消防队1号站担任志愿消防员。“我做志愿者是为了回馈邻里，但与队友一起走进体育场，是为了纪念那天毫不犹豫冲上塔楼楼梯的人们。

这次攀登既是一次庄严的致敬，也强化了作战战备。医疗后勤人员肩负着在多域作战中为部队提供持续保障的任务，这一使命要求在争夺激烈、条件严酷的环境中分发救生医疗设备与物资时具备规划能力和心理韧性。

AMLC和第六医疗后勤管理中心人员克服疲惫，共同冲过体育场终点线，从而进一步巩固了陆军与保护美国社区、守护国土的平民一线应急人员之间历久弥坚的纽带。

这次活动考验了我们的耐力，同时增强了我们的团队精神，并证明战备不仅限于我们日常的案头工作，还延伸到我们工作之外的活动以及我们所支持的社区，”戈麦斯说。

AMLC总部位于德特里克堡，是陆军的第八类医疗物资司令部，提供一体化医疗后勤，支撑陆军和联合部队从战略支援区域到战术前沿的战备。

第6医疗后勤管理中心也总部位于德特里克堡，是一支专业部队，采用分基地行动，提供前沿和集中化医疗物资管理、战区级配送跟踪以及作战后勤同步，以支援全球各地的作战指挥官。

items.title: What Will a Growing MQ-9 Presence in Latin America Mean for SOUTHCOM?
items.author: Todd South
items.summary: A reported surge of MQ-9 Reaper drones to Latin America could widen the scope of intelligence gathering and free up more strike options against cartels in the region, experts tell Air & Space Forces Magazine. The post What Will a Growing MQ-9 Presence in Latin America Mean for SOUTHCOM? appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
A reported surge of MQ-9 Reaper drones to Latin America could widen the scope of intelligence gathering and free up more strike options against cartels in the region, experts tell Air & Space Forces Magazine.

According to numerous media reports, the Pentagon has supplied Colombia and Ecuador with several Reapers and transferred an undisclosed number of MQ-9s from U.S. Africa Command to U.S. Southern Command.

Officials from Colombia and Ecuador have confirmed they are receiving MQ-9s to local media outlets, and CNN, the New York Times, and the Wall Street Journal have all reported that Reapers are moving from Africa to Central and South America.

Spokespeople from AFRICOM and SOUTHCOM both declined to comment on the movement of any aircraft, but the reports indicate how Reapers, long known for their role in counterinsurgency operations in the Middle East and Africa, are becoming more and more important to the U.S. military’s counter-narcotics efforts.

“We’re helping our partners build up their capabilities, and then that allows us to kind of push more resources into countries with fewer capabilities,” Henry Ziemer, an associate fellow with the Center for Strategic and International Studies Americas Program, told Air & Space Forces Magazine.

Marine Corps Gen. Francis L. Donovan, head of SOUTHCOM, has made a point of emphasizing the use of unmanned, autonomous systems in the region since taking command in February.

“U.S. Southern Command is focusing on integrating autonomous warfare systems to enhance domain awareness across maritime, air, and border areas,” SOUTHCOM spokesperson Steven McCloud told Air & Space Forces Magazine in an email. “These unmanned systems allow our partners to monitor their territory better and facilitate informed interdiction decisions. Improved data flows and situational awareness benefit everyone.”

SOUTHCOM established an Autonomous Warfare Command in April to lead its efforts on that front.

Any increase in the number of long-endurance intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance platforms in SOUTHCOM—both piloted and remotely piloted—will give the combatant commander more options and allow them to share intelligence with their counterparts, retired Air Force Maj. Gen. Julian “Ghost” Cheater told Air & Space Forces Magazine.

And demand for intel is surging amid a growing effort to combat the cartels and the flow of drugs in the region, led by President Donald Trump and boosted by allies and partners in the region.

Beginning in March, a U.S.-led effort helped create the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, which has grown from an initial dozen members to 19 nations, with Colombia being the most recent. In August, SOUTHCOM announced its new Joint Task Force-Western Hemisphere, the region’s “action arm” for missions like counter-narcotics.

At the time, former Air Forces Southern Commander Lt. Gen. Norm Seip told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the new task force could lead to more prioritization of assets for the SOUTHCOM commander.

Cheater, who retired in June and most recently served as the director of strategy, policy, and plans for SOUTHCOM, added that any new allocation of ISR assets would be based on the combatant commander’s priorities—which would suggest Donovan is putting an emphasis on intelligence gathering.

“Ultimately, AFSOUTH is responsible for providing that comprehensive command and control of airborne operations in theater,” said Cheater, who has more than 3,700 flight hours, a good chunk of that on drones, and commanded drone units such as the 432nd Wing out of Creech Air Force Base, Nev. “This component reports directly to the combatant commander, and if AFSOC or another entity provides those assets, those are generally commanded and controlled via AFSOUTH.”

In addition to the reported MQ-9 transfers, SOUTHCOM also announced in mid-September the sale of more than $6 million worth of K1000 ultra-long endurance drones to Panama to “monitor remote borders, safeguard strategic maritime corridors, and dismantle illicit drug trafficking and human smuggling networks,” according to a command release.

Built by Kraus Hamdani Aerospace, the K1000 is a 45-pound, 9.8-foot-long drone with a 16.4-foot wingspan that can reach speeds up to 75 miles per hour and has a ceiling of 20,000 feet. It can fly continuously for 24 hours in its solar-recharge configuration or 12 hours in its electronic vertical take-off and landing configuration. It has a range of about 1,000 miles and can be controlled via line of sight comms within 90 miles or beyond line of sight using satellite comms. A three-person crew can pack it into Pelican cases in under 15 minutes.

The Reaper’s airframe costs between $30 and $50 million each; sensors and weapons can add to that cost. It is a medium-to-high-altitude, long-endurance drone with a 66-foot wingspan and a 50,000-foot ceiling. The drone can fly for 27 continuous hours and up to 42 hours in extended-range variants with a range of 1,000 to 1,400 nautical miles. It has similar line of sight/beyond line of sight command and control capabilities to the K1000.

As of Sept. 30, 2025, the Air Force reported 182 Reapers in its inventory, though at least 45 have been lost during operations against Iran.

As operations in SOUTHCOM have ramped up under the Trump administration, the MQ-9 has already played a role.

Since September 2025, SOUTHCOM has conducted at least 71 lethal, kinetic strikes targeting alleged drug boats. The strikes, some of which have reportedly been made with MQ-9s, have killed at least 215 people, with another 17 missing or presumed dead, according to government accounts and media reports.

The strikes have mostly targeted vessels near Venezuela’s shores, in the Pacific Ocean, and across the Caribbean. Early strikes began before the Pentagon formally announced Operation Southern Spear in November 2025, the wider effort to target cartel assets with kinetic strikes and other means. That temporary operation has become the more permanent JTF-WH.

Drug Boat Strikes

Those strikes have sparked intense debate among legal experts and lawmakers, and the Washington Post reported in July that a Drug Enforcement Administration assessment found that they have not been effective in stemming the flow of cocaine into the U.S.

Ben Friedman, policy director at Defense Priorities, a D.C.-based think tank that promotes a restrained U.S. foreign policy, told Air & Space Forces Magazine that he doubts the strikes will ever be effective.

“I don’t think it—using military forces to counter the flow of narcotics—works particularly well, and we have decades of experience at that. Even if we intensify it, I think we’ll get the same result at a higher price,” Friedman said.

During Congressional testimony in March, Donovan indicated that SOUTHCOM is shifting to take a more comprehensive approach to the counter-cartel fight.

“We’ve seen changes in the narco-traffickers’ patterns, and in a closed setting I’d like to provide some more details specifically on that, but … the boat strikes aren’t the answer,” Donovan told Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) on March 19.

“What we’re moving for right now [is] … really a counter-cartel campaign process that puts total systemic friction across this network,” Donovan added.

More MQ-9s in theater could aid this expanded effort.

Currently, Reapers are tasked out of various locations, including U.S. facilities in Puerto Rico. And while the platform has a long loiter time, its eye-in-the-sky is not infinite. Having Reapers actually located in Ecuador and Colombia extends the regional reach by freeing up assets for other operations with other partners.

“These drones to SOUTHCOM, they can also be operated out of Colombia. I think the drones of Panama [are] really going to help find the targets that they’re looking for, targets being drug traffickers,” Wilder Alejandro Sanchez, president of the D.C.-based consulting firm Second Floor Strategies and nonresident senior associate at the CSIS Americas program, told Air & Space Forces Magazine.

Potential MQ-9 Operating Locations

Ziemer said increased use of drones like the MQ-9 will widen the ISR and data and communications sharing between the United States and regional allies and partners.

“Long-endurance UASs are tremendously useful to patrol large swaths of the jungle, patrol large maritime borders, looking for illicit activity,” Ziemer said.

That can include illegal mining and fishing, human trafficking and a host of other nefarious cartel and criminal organization or foreign terrorist organization practices, Ziemer said.

Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Mark “Chris” Nowland, former deputy chief of staff for operations and commander of Air Forces Southern, told Air & Space Forces Magazine that the airborne assets will prove vital for building “patterns of life” on cartel activities.

“The advantage of the Reaper being there is it gives you this incredible distance that you can cover now and put ISR on,” Nowland said. “Now you just have something that you can cue and go and get better vigilance on or discover new stuff that you couldn’t because of the sensor capabilities they have.”

While the experts and former military officials lauded the increased capabilities the new MQ-9s could bring, they also noted limitations and risks with the move.

Sanchez, a Peruvian native, and Ziemer agreed that MQ-9s are not the only drones needed. Long-endurance, high-altitude drones play a crucial role, Sanchez said, but under the canopy of dense jungles or on remote mountaintops, smaller, nimbler, backpack-portable drones already feature in counter-narcotics operations and will become even more necessary.

“It’s not just big, expensive Reapers or MQ-4 Tritons, but also small … [drones] that they can transport in a backpack, so the small squads can deploy them and find the objective much faster when they’re on the ground,” Sanchez said.

Sanchez also noted that regardless of the platform, communication and intel sharing must ramp up, which will require building that capacity within under-resourced partner nations.

“Imagine the Reaper drone has some information. It’s going to be sent to a base … and then how long does it take for that information to be sent to the troops, who need to go to that location?” Sanchez asked.

Presuming Reapers operate out of partner bases, they face their own dangers, Nowland added.

“If these U.S. assets are effective, [they] could become targets,” Nowland said. “So how do you protect them wherever you put them…? This is a dilemma that I’m sure SOUTHCOM is thinking about.”

Friedman also worries that with a change in government, assets sold or given to partner nations could be used for unintended measures.

“South American politics are not nearly as unstable as they used to be, but there are changes of government, changes of leadership, even the potential for coups,” he said. “They might be doing things that lack discretion and control… to see a South American government just doing the kind of drone strikes that we do against their own populations with capability that we gave them.”

More broadly, Friedman argued that the overall push of military assets in Latin America is an escalation in the region and threatens to make the decadeslong Drug War into a literal war.

“I don’t see a lot of virtue in having a more militarized approach to the Western Hemisphere,” said Friedman. “In practice, I think you wind up doing a bunch of things if you’re doing it with the Pentagon that probably don’t make sense.”

“If I had my druthers, they’d probably be using [them] more for training in the United States and not either of these missions,” he said. “You know, preparing for a war that actually involves some kind of core U.S. interest.”

- On Jan. 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order declaring cartels Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and asserting that the U.S. is in a “non-international armed conflict” with drug-trafficking entities.

- On Sept. 2, 2025, Trump and SOUTHCOM confirmed the first lethal drug boat strike, saying it killed 11 individuals belonging to the Tren de Aragua gang.

- In December 2025, the Trump administration released a new National Defense Strategy and National Security Strategy prioritizing the Western Hemisphere and military actions against drug cartels, including “targeted deployments to secure the border and defeat cartels, including where necessary the use of lethal force to replace the failed law enforcement-only strategy of the last several decades.”

- On March 5, 2026, at a Americas Counter Cartel Coalition conference, Trump said the U.S. will work with Latin American countries “to do whatever we have to do. We’ll use missiles. … But we’ll do whatever you need. The only way to defeat these enemies is by unleashing the power of our militaries.”
items.summaryZh: 专家告诉《空天力量》杂志，据报大量MQ-9“死神”无人机涌入拉丁美洲，可能扩大情报搜集范围，并为打击该地区贩毒集团腾出更多打击选项。《MQ-9在拉丁美洲日益增长的存在对美军南方司令部意味着什么？》一文最初发表于《空天力量》杂志。
items.titleZh: MQ-9在拉丁美洲日益增长的存在对美军南方司令部意味着什么？
zhParas: 专家告诉《空天力量》杂志，据报大量MQ-9“死神”无人机涌入拉丁美洲，可能扩大情报搜集范围，并为打击该地区贩毒集团腾出更多打击选项。
据多家媒体报道，五角大楼已向哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔提供了数架“死神”无人机，并将数量不详的MQ-9无人机从美军非洲司令部转移到美军南方司令部。
哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔官员已向当地媒体证实，他们正在接收MQ-9无人机；CNN、《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》均报道称，“死神”无人机正从非洲转移至中美洲和南美洲。
美国非洲司令部和南方司令部的发言人均拒绝就任何飞机的调动置评，但这些报道表明，长期以来以在中东和非洲执行反叛乱行动而闻名的“死神”无人机，正对美国军方的禁毒工作变得越来越重要。
我们正在帮助伙伴提升能力，这样一来，我们就能把更多资源投入到能力较弱的国家，”战略与国际研究中心美洲项目副研究员亨利·齐默对《空军与太空军杂志》表示。
美国南方司令部司令、海军陆战队上将弗朗西斯·L·多诺万自2月上任以来，一直强调在该地区使用无人和自主系统。
美国南方司令部正专注于整合自主作战系统，以增强海上、空中和边境地区的领域感知能力，”美国南方司令部发言人史蒂文·麦克劳德在电子邮件中告诉《空军与太空军杂志》。“这些无人系统使我们的伙伴能够更好地监视其领土，并有助于做出有依据的拦截决策。改进的数据流和态势感知惠及各方。
美军南方司令部于4月成立了一个自主作战司令部，以领导其在这一领域的工作。
退役空军少将朱利安·“幽灵”·奇特告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，美军南方司令部任何长航时情报、监视与侦察平台——无论有人驾驶还是遥控驾驶——数量的增加，都将为该作战司令部司令提供更多选择，并使其能够与同行分享情报。
随着在该地区打击贩毒集团和毒品流动的努力不断加强——这一努力由唐纳德·特朗普总统领导，并得到该地区盟友和伙伴的支持——对情报的需求正在激增。
从3月开始，一项由美国主导的努力帮助创建了美洲反卡特尔联盟，该联盟已从最初的12个成员扩大到19个国家，哥伦比亚是最近加入的。8月，美军南方司令部宣布成立新的西半球联合特遣部队，作为该地区执行禁毒等任务的“行动臂”。
当时，前南方空军司令部司令诺姆·塞普中将告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，这支新成立的特遣部队可能促使更多资产向美军南方司令部司令倾斜。
6月退役、最近担任美军南方司令部战略、政策与计划主任的奇特尔补充说，任何新的情报、监视与侦察（ISR）资产分配都将以作战司令部司令的优先事项为依据——这表明多诺万正把重点放在情报搜集上。
归根结底，南方空军负责提供战区空中行动的全面指挥与控制，”奇特尔说。他拥有超过3700个飞行小时，其中很大一部分是在无人机上，并曾指挥过无人机部队，例如内华达州克里奇空军基地的第432联队。“该组成部分直接向作战司令部司令汇报，如果空军特种作战司令部或其他实体提供这些资产，它们通常通过南方空军进行指挥与控制。
除了有报道的MQ-9转移外，美军南方司令部还在9月中旬宣布，向巴拿马出售价值超过600万美元的K1000超长航时无人机，以“监控偏远边境、保卫战略海上走廊，并瓦解非法毒品贩运和人口走私网络”，据该司令部的一份新闻稿称。
K1000无人机由Kraus Hamdani Aerospace制造，重45磅，长9.8英尺，翼展16.4英尺，最高时速可达75英里，升限为20,000英尺。在太阳能充电构型下，它可连续飞行24小时；在电动垂直起降构型下，可连续飞行12小时。其航程约为1,000英里，可在90英里内通过视距通信控制，或使用卫星通信进行超视距控制。一个三人机组可在15分钟内将其装入Pelican箱。
死神”无人机的机体单价在3000万至5000万美元之间；传感器和武器还会增加这一成本。它是一款中高空、长航时无人机，翼展66英尺，升限5万英尺。该无人机可连续飞行27小时，增程型最长可飞行42小时，航程为1000至1400海里。其视距/超视距指挥控制能力与K1000类似。
截至2025年9月30日，美国空军报告其库存中有182架“死神”无人机，不过在对伊朗的行动中至少损失了45架。
随着特朗普政府时期美军南方司令部的行动不断加强，MQ-9已经发挥了作用。
自2025年9月以来，美国南方司令部至少实施了71次针对涉嫌运毒船只的致命性动能打击。据报道，其中一些打击由MQ-9无人机实施；据政府通报和媒体报道，这些打击已造成至少215人死亡，另有17人失踪或推定死亡。
这些打击主要针对委内瑞拉海岸附近、太平洋以及加勒比海各地的船只。早期打击始于五角大楼于2025年11月正式宣布“南方长矛行动”之前；该行动是一项更广泛的努力，旨在通过动能打击和其他手段打击贩毒集团资产。那项临时行动已成为更为常设的联合特遣部队-西半球（JTF-WH）。
打击毒品船只
这些打击在法律专家和议员中引发了激烈辩论，而《华盛顿邮报》7月报道称，美国缉毒局的一项评估发现，这些打击并未有效遏制可卡因流入美国。
位于华盛顿、主张美国奉行克制外交政策的智库“国防优先事项”政策主任本·弗里德曼对《空军与太空军杂志》表示，他怀疑这些打击永远不会奏效。
我不认为——动用军事力量来遏制毒品流动——效果会特别好，而且我们在这方面有几十年的经验。即使我们加大力度，我认为我们也只会付出更高代价，却得到同样的结果，”弗里德曼说。
在3月的国会作证中，多诺万表示，美军南方司令部正转向采取更全面的方式来打击贩毒集团。
我们已经看到毒品贩运者的活动模式发生了变化，在闭门场合中，我想就此具体提供更多细节，但……打击船只并非解决之道，”多诺万在3月19日对参议员马克·凯利（亚利桑那州民主党人）说。
我们眼下正在推动的……实际上是一个反贩毒集团战役进程，旨在让整个网络承受全面的系统性摩擦，”多诺万补充说。
战区内更多MQ-9无人机可能有助于这项扩大的行动。
目前，“死神”无人机以多个地点为基地执行任务，包括波多黎各的美军设施。尽管该平台拥有较长滞空时间，但其“空中之眼”并非无限。让“死神”无人机实际部署在厄瓜多尔和哥伦比亚，可扩大区域覆盖范围，并腾出资源用于与其他伙伴开展的其他行动。

专家告诉《空天力量》杂志，据报大量MQ-9“死神”无人机涌入拉丁美洲，可能扩大情报搜集范围，并为打击该地区贩毒集团腾出更多打击选项。

据多家媒体报道，五角大楼已向哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔提供了数架“死神”无人机，并将数量不详的MQ-9无人机从美军非洲司令部转移到美军南方司令部。

哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔官员已向当地媒体证实，他们正在接收MQ-9无人机；CNN、《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》均报道称，“死神”无人机正从非洲转移至中美洲和南美洲。

美国非洲司令部和南方司令部的发言人均拒绝就任何飞机的调动置评，但这些报道表明，长期以来以在中东和非洲执行反叛乱行动而闻名的“死神”无人机，正对美国军方的禁毒工作变得越来越重要。

我们正在帮助伙伴提升能力，这样一来，我们就能把更多资源投入到能力较弱的国家，”战略与国际研究中心美洲项目副研究员亨利·齐默对《空军与太空军杂志》表示。

美国南方司令部司令、海军陆战队上将弗朗西斯·L·多诺万自2月上任以来，一直强调在该地区使用无人和自主系统。

美国南方司令部正专注于整合自主作战系统，以增强海上、空中和边境地区的领域感知能力，”美国南方司令部发言人史蒂文·麦克劳德在电子邮件中告诉《空军与太空军杂志》。“这些无人系统使我们的伙伴能够更好地监视其领土，并有助于做出有依据的拦截决策。改进的数据流和态势感知惠及各方。

美军南方司令部于4月成立了一个自主作战司令部，以领导其在这一领域的工作。

退役空军少将朱利安·“幽灵”·奇特告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，美军南方司令部任何长航时情报、监视与侦察平台——无论有人驾驶还是遥控驾驶——数量的增加，都将为该作战司令部司令提供更多选择，并使其能够与同行分享情报。

随着在该地区打击贩毒集团和毒品流动的努力不断加强——这一努力由唐纳德·特朗普总统领导，并得到该地区盟友和伙伴的支持——对情报的需求正在激增。

从3月开始，一项由美国主导的努力帮助创建了美洲反卡特尔联盟，该联盟已从最初的12个成员扩大到19个国家，哥伦比亚是最近加入的。8月，美军南方司令部宣布成立新的西半球联合特遣部队，作为该地区执行禁毒等任务的“行动臂”。

当时，前南方空军司令部司令诺姆·塞普中将告诉《空军与太空军杂志》，这支新成立的特遣部队可能促使更多资产向美军南方司令部司令倾斜。

6月退役、最近担任美军南方司令部战略、政策与计划主任的奇特尔补充说，任何新的情报、监视与侦察（ISR）资产分配都将以作战司令部司令的优先事项为依据——这表明多诺万正把重点放在情报搜集上。

归根结底，南方空军负责提供战区空中行动的全面指挥与控制，”奇特尔说。他拥有超过3700个飞行小时，其中很大一部分是在无人机上，并曾指挥过无人机部队，例如内华达州克里奇空军基地的第432联队。“该组成部分直接向作战司令部司令汇报，如果空军特种作战司令部或其他实体提供这些资产，它们通常通过南方空军进行指挥与控制。

除了有报道的MQ-9转移外，美军南方司令部还在9月中旬宣布，向巴拿马出售价值超过600万美元的K1000超长航时无人机，以“监控偏远边境、保卫战略海上走廊，并瓦解非法毒品贩运和人口走私网络”，据该司令部的一份新闻稿称。

K1000无人机由Kraus Hamdani Aerospace制造，重45磅，长9.8英尺，翼展16.4英尺，最高时速可达75英里，升限为20,000英尺。在太阳能充电构型下，它可连续飞行24小时；在电动垂直起降构型下，可连续飞行12小时。其航程约为1,000英里，可在90英里内通过视距通信控制，或使用卫星通信进行超视距控制。一个三人机组可在15分钟内将其装入Pelican箱。

死神”无人机的机体单价在3000万至5000万美元之间；传感器和武器还会增加这一成本。它是一款中高空、长航时无人机，翼展66英尺，升限5万英尺。该无人机可连续飞行27小时，增程型最长可飞行42小时，航程为1000至1400海里。其视距/超视距指挥控制能力与K1000类似。

截至2025年9月30日，美国空军报告其库存中有182架“死神”无人机，不过在对伊朗的行动中至少损失了45架。

随着特朗普政府时期美军南方司令部的行动不断加强，MQ-9已经发挥了作用。

自2025年9月以来，美国南方司令部至少实施了71次针对涉嫌运毒船只的致命性动能打击。据报道，其中一些打击由MQ-9无人机实施；据政府通报和媒体报道，这些打击已造成至少215人死亡，另有17人失踪或推定死亡。

这些打击主要针对委内瑞拉海岸附近、太平洋以及加勒比海各地的船只。早期打击始于五角大楼于2025年11月正式宣布“南方长矛行动”之前；该行动是一项更广泛的努力，旨在通过动能打击和其他手段打击贩毒集团资产。那项临时行动已成为更为常设的联合特遣部队-西半球（JTF-WH）。

这些打击在法律专家和议员中引发了激烈辩论，而《华盛顿邮报》7月报道称，美国缉毒局的一项评估发现，这些打击并未有效遏制可卡因流入美国。

位于华盛顿、主张美国奉行克制外交政策的智库“国防优先事项”政策主任本·弗里德曼对《空军与太空军杂志》表示，他怀疑这些打击永远不会奏效。

我不认为——动用军事力量来遏制毒品流动——效果会特别好，而且我们在这方面有几十年的经验。即使我们加大力度，我认为我们也只会付出更高代价，却得到同样的结果，”弗里德曼说。

在3月的国会作证中，多诺万表示，美军南方司令部正转向采取更全面的方式来打击贩毒集团。

我们已经看到毒品贩运者的活动模式发生了变化，在闭门场合中，我想就此具体提供更多细节，但……打击船只并非解决之道，”多诺万在3月19日对参议员马克·凯利（亚利桑那州民主党人）说。

我们眼下正在推动的……实际上是一个反贩毒集团战役进程，旨在让整个网络承受全面的系统性摩擦，”多诺万补充说。

2026年3月5日，在美洲反卡特尔联盟会议上，特朗普表示，美国将与拉丁美洲国家合作，“做我们必须做的事。我们会使用导弹。……但我们会做你们需要的一切。击败这些敌人的唯一办法，就是释放我们军队的力量。
